item.title: 2027: BTO coalition reaffirms support for Tinubu’s re-election
item.description: …Group hails Akure presidential rally, pledges sustained grassroots mobilisation By Dayo Johnson, Akure The National President of the BTO Coalition Platform for PBAT 2027, Otunba Adeshina Abubakar Omoluabi, has reaffirmed the group’s support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid ahead of the 2027 general elections. Omoluabi also commended the presidential rally held in Akure, Ondo State, where Tinubu was represented by Vice-President Kashim Shettima. Other prominent attendees included the APC National Chairman, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda; Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign, former Zamfara State Governor Abdulaziz Yari; Chairman of the Progressive Governors Forum, Governor Hope Uzodimma; serving and former governors, ministers and other party chieftains. Omoluabi said the coalition joined APC leaders, stakeholders and supporters at the rally as part of ongoing mobilisation efforts ahead of the elections. He said the coalition’s participation was led by him as its national president, alongside members and supporters of the platform. According to him, their presence underscored the group’s involvement in the broader political activities and engagements ahead of the 2027 elections. The rally, organised by the Minister of Interior, Dr. Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, brought together party leaders, stakeholders, supporters and various political groups to demonstrate their support for Tinubu’s re-election. For the BTO Coalition Platform, Omoluabi said participation in the Akure rally formed part of its ongoing political engagement and commitment to supporting the Tinubu administration’s continuity beyond 2027. He added that the platform’s presence reflected its determination to work with other APC stakeholders and participate in activities aimed at strengthening political engagement, collaboration and grassroots mobilisation across communities. Omoluabi said the coalition recognised the importance of sustained participation and organised engagement in the political process. He added that its activities ahead of the elections would focus on stakeholder engagement, grassroots participation and collaboration with relevant political structures. The coalition reaffirmed its commitment to remaining actively involved in political engagements in line with its objectives, expressing readiness to sustain its participation as preparations for the 2027 elections continue. “The Akure rally marks another opportunity to engage with party stakeholders and demonstrate our presence within the wider APC political community,” Omoluabi said. item.title: Court orders Maina’s son to serve seven-year jail term
item.description: …..Faisal to serve sentence concurrently from October 14 re-arrest A Federal High Court in Abuja has ordered the remand of Faisal Maina, son of former Chairman of the defunct Pension Reform Task Team, Abdulrasheed Maina, in a correctional centre to serve his seven-year jail term for money laundering. Justice James Omotosho made the order on Thursday after granting an ex parte application filed by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC). The commission had asked the court to issue a warrant committing Faisal to the Nigeria Correctional Service (NCoS) to enforce the judgment convicting him of money laundering and failure to make full disclosure in an asset declaration form. Faisal was arrested by the Department of State Services (DSS) on October 14 in the Karsana area of Abuja, about six years after he jumped bail and absconded from trial. He was subsequently handed over to the EFCC. In its application, the commission also sought an order directing that his prison sentence should commence from October 14, the date of his re-arrest. After the EFCC’s lawyer, M.K. Hussain, moved the application, Justice Omotosho granted the reliefs sought and issued a warrant for Faisal’s commitment to a correctional centre. The judge ordered that, in line with the Court of Appeal’s judgment of November 24, 2022, Faisal should serve three years’ imprisonment on count one, seven years on count two and three years on count three. The sentences are to run concurrently, beginning from October 14, 2026, when he was re-arrested. Faisal was arraigned before the Federal High Court in Abuja in 2019 on a three-count charge bordering on money laundering and failure to fully disclose his assets. He pleaded not guilty to the charges before Justice Okon Abang, who was then presiding over the case, but later jumped bail and stopped attending court proceedings. Following his disappearance, Abang proceeded with the trial in his absence and convicted him on October 7, 2021. The court initially sentenced him to five years’ imprisonment on counts one and three, and 14 years on count two, with the sentences to run concurrently. Abang also ordered that Faisal be arrested wherever he was found and taken to a correctional centre to serve his sentence. However, the Court of Appeal subsequently upheld the conviction but reduced the sentences in its judgment delivered on November 24, 2022, to three years on counts one and three, and seven years on count two. Faisal’s father, Abdulrasheed, was also convicted in a separate money laundering case involving about N2 billion. He has since completed his prison term. item.title: BOA earmarks N200bn for 400,000 dry-season farmers
item.description: …..FMN targets five tonnes of wheat per hectare in 2026/2027 farming season By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse The Bank of Agriculture (BOA) has earmarked about N200 billion to finance dry-season agricultural activities for 400,000 farmers across Nigeria as part of efforts to boost domestic food production and strengthen food security. The North-West Zonal Manager of the bank, Abdul-Razaq Datti Saleh, disclosed this at the flag-off of the 2026/2027 dry-season wheat farming programme organised in partnership with Flour Mills of Nigeria (FMN) at Maje Village, Taura Local Government Area of Jigawa State. Saleh explained that the financing would be channelled through farmer aggregator companies to enable individual farmers to access support for land preparation, irrigation, improved seeds, fertilisers and other essential agricultural inputs. He said the partnership with FMN was aimed at increasing domestic wheat production, reducing Nigeria’s dependence on imported wheat and strengthening food security. According to him, wheat remains an important raw material for households and industries, adding that expanding local production would create employment opportunities, increase farmers’ incomes and strengthen rural economies. Also speaking, the General Manager of Golden Agro Input Limited (GAIL), a subsidiary of FMN Agro, Engineer Tayo Ilori, said the company was supporting 10,000 farmers across six states under the 2026 dry-season wheat programme. He explained that each participating farmer received agricultural inputs for one hectare, comprising 100 kilogrammes of wheat seeds, six bags of urea, four bags of NPK 20:10:5 fertiliser and chemicals for weed and pest control. Ilori estimated the value of the input package at between N250,000 and N350,000 per hectare. He said the inputs were provided as loans, which farmers would repay with harvested wheat grains at prevailing market prices rather than through cash payments. Ilori identified improved seeds, quality fertilisers and regular extension services as critical factors in increasing wheat productivity. He added that GAIL had deployed about 250 lead outgrowers to provide technical guidance and support to participating farmers across the six states. The company, he said, was targeting a yield of seven metric tonnes per hectare in the 2026/2027 season, expressing confidence that the target was achievable through the adoption of modern farming practices. The Project Director, Engineer Olusegun Falade, said the programme had raised average wheat productivity from less than one tonne per hectare at its inception to about 4.2 tonnes, with some farmers recording yields of up to 7.2 tonnes. Falade identified farmers’ reluctance to repay loans, slow adoption of improved farming practices and land ownership challenges as some of the obstacles confronting the programme. item.title: Obidient Movement congratulates Yunusa Tanko on appointment as SDP presidential campaign DG
item.description: The Obidient Movement has congratulated its former National Coordinator, Dr Yunusa Tanko, on his appointment as National Coordinator of the Social Democratic Party’s Presidential Campaign Council ahead of the 2027 general elections. The movement described the appointment as recognition of Tanko’s political experience, organisational skills and contributions to the struggle for a better Nigeria. In a statement issued on Wednesday by its Media and Communications Directorate, the group wished him success in his new role, saying his emergence reflected the leadership capacity developed within the movement. It said Tanko’s appointment, despite his move to a different political platform, should be seen as an opportunity for collaboration rather than a source of division. The movement explained that its membership extended beyond party lines, bringing together Nigerians from different ethnic, religious and social backgrounds around the shared aspiration for competent and accountable leadership. While encouraging its members to join the Nigeria Democratic Congress, the party of its principal, Peter Obi, it said it recognised that its supporters belonged to different political parties. “Consequently, the emergence of leaders from our Movement into influential positions across different political platforms should be a source of pride, not division,” the statement said. The group also cited Obi’s attendance at the inauguration of the presidential campaign office of Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, as an example of his belief in cooperation across political differences. According to the movement, Obi has consistently maintained that national interest should take precedence over partisan considerations. It added that its objective was not to confine capable Nigerians to one political party but to develop leaders who could contribute to national development wherever they found themselves. Tanko was on Wednesday unveiled as the SDP’s national presidential campaign coordinator during the inauguration of the party’s campaign council in Abuja. He pledged to work with the party’s presidential candidate, Adewale Adebayo, and his running mate, Usman Bugaje, ahead of the 2027 elections. The appointment followed Tanko’s resignation as political adviser (North) to Obi, which he said took effect on October 30. item.title: Why I backed Tinubu in 2023 but will challenge him in 2027 — Makinde
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Three years after supporting President Bola Tinubu’s emergence in 2023, Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, has explained why he is challenging him in the 2027 presidential election, citing four major concerns about the administration. Makinde, the presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), said his decision was not driven by a personal disagreement with Tinubu or an ambition to occupy Aso Rock, but by what he described as concerns about Nigeria’s future. The governor stated this in a newsletter on Thursday, recalling that he backed Tinubu because he believed the president could unite Nigerians, build a government based on competence and address the country’s economic challenges. He said, “I supported President Tinubu in 2023 because I believed his experience and political relationships could help him bring Nigerians together. “One thing I have always acknowledged about him is his ability to build bridges across political divides. I believed he could use that ability to establish a government of national unity and competence, focused on improving the lives of Nigerians.” Makinde identified four major reasons for his decision to challenge Tinubu, beginning with what he described as “economic stability without economic development.” While acknowledging improvements in some macroeconomic indicators, he said such gains had not translated into better living conditions for ordinary Nigerians. “Also, contrary to the formula President Tinubu claims to be following, economic stabilisation and development are not necessarily sequential. Nigerians did not have to endure this level of hardship while waiting for development to begin,” he added. His second concern was what he described as “governing by excuses”, accusing the administration of repeatedly citing inherited challenges instead of showing measurable progress in tackling them. “Every government inherits problems, but it is elected to solve them. Over three years into this administration, we are still hearing explanations about inherited poverty, insecurity, electricity problems and other challenges, when Nigerians should be seeing more measurable progress towards resolving them.” On national unity, the governor said he had expected Tinubu’s political experience and ability to build alliances to produce a government that brought capable Nigerians together. “Instead, I have come to believe that his political alliances serve his political objectives more than the national interest, and I am deeply concerned about the weakening of opposition parties, which are essential to a functioning democracy,” Makinde said. His fourth concern was “economic reforms without adequate protection for Nigerians.” Although he supported reforms to the petrol subsidy and foreign exchange systems, Makinde said the government should have prepared measures to protect citizens from the resulting hardship. item.title: Oil wells verification to ensure fair sharing of 13% derivation fund — RMAFC
item.description: By Emmanuel Iheaka The Revenue Mobilisation, Allocation and Fiscal Commission (RMAFC) has said the ongoing verification of oil and gas wells across the country is aimed at ensuring equitable distribution of the 13 per cent derivation fund among producing states. The Chairman of the Commission and Chairman of the Executive Committee of the Inter-Agency Technical Committee (IATC), Dr. Mohammed Shehu, stated this in Owerri, Imo State, during the flag-off of a field verification exercise covering disputed and newly drilled crude oil and gas wells. Shehu said the commission was constitutionally empowered to ensure the equitable disbursement of the 13 per cent derivation fund to oil and gas-producing states. He explained that the reconstituted IATC convened in Owerri to formally commence the verification exercise covering disputed and newly drilled crude oil and gas wells from 2017 to date. According to him, the committee’s terms of reference include examining and verifying the coordinates of disputed and newly drilled oil and gas wells, conducting physical inspections of the affected wells and ensuring the accurate plotting of verified coordinates. He said the committee was also mandated to ensure that only approved maps were used in plotting coordinates and that relevant court decisions were considered in resolving disputes involving oil and gas wells. Other responsibilities, he said, include submitting its findings and reports exclusively to RMAFC for ratification and adoption, as well as addressing other related matters arising from its field operations. Shehu described the exercise as a crucial step towards ensuring statutory accuracy, technical reliability and fiscal equity in the Federation Account allocation framework. He said the determination of the exact coordinates and geographical positions of oil and gas wellheads directly affected the legal and financial entitlements of the respective sub-national entities. The RMAFC chairman consequently charged all technical officers deployed for the exercise to carry out the national assignment with diligence, technical precision and professionalism. He stressed that every verified coordinate, technical assessment and physical observation made during the exercise must be capable of withstanding rigorous statutory scrutiny. Shehu further directed that the harmonised technical report be submitted exclusively to the commission for administrative processing and formal adoption. item.title: Gunmen kill young man near Imo varsity in Owerri
item.description: By Emmanuel Iheaka Unidentified gunmen have shot dead a young man suspected to be a student near the Bishop’s Court area, close to the Imo State University, Owerri. The attackers reportedly stormed a car wash facility in the area in a Lexus Jeep and opened fire on the victim before fleeing the scene. The incident threw residents and business operators in the area into panic, as people scampered for safety following the shooting. An eyewitness said the assailants initially appeared to have brought their vehicle for washing before launching the attack. “They came to a car spot in a Lexus Jeep, acting as if they wanted to wash the car. The next we heard was a gunshot, and the young man was in a pool of blood. They zoomed off. Nobody can actually say what led to the attack,” the source said. The motive for the killing was yet to be established as of the time of filing this report. The incident comes amid reports of clashes between rival cult groups in parts of Imo State, which have reportedly claimed lives in the past month. The police had about three weeks ago announced the arrest of some suspects in connection with the attacks, adding that investigations were ongoing to apprehend other persons involved. In response to the security concerns, the Commissioner of Police in the state, CP Audu Garba Bosso, convened a strategic security meeting on October 18, 2026, with Area Commanders, Divisional Police Officers and Tactical Team Commanders to assess the situation and strengthen security operations across the state. Following the meeting, operational commanders were directed to intensify intelligence-led operations, conduct targeted raids on identified criminal hideouts, strengthen patrols in security hotspots and respond promptly to emerging threats. The commissioner also directed closer collaboration with community leaders, youth groups and other stakeholders to improve intelligence gathering and prevent further violence. However, the Police Public Relations Officer in the state, Henry Okoye, was yet to react to the latest killing as of the time of filing this report. item.title: 2027: Reps condemn political violence, launch probe
item.description: …Agbedi cites killings, attacks in Enugu, Katsina, Nasarawa, Delta By Gift Chapi Odekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has condemned reported cases of political violence, attacks and disruption of political activities across the country ahead of the 2027 general elections, resolving to investigate the incidents. The resolution followed the adoption of a motion of urgent public importance sponsored by the House Minority Leader, Rep. Fred Agbedi, and 16 other lawmakers on Wednesday, amid growing concerns over attacks on political meetings, rallies and processions in different parts of the country. Presenting the motion on behalf of the sponsors, Agbedi condemned acts of violence, intimidation, assault and destruction of property associated with political rallies, meetings, processions and other lawful political activities, irrespective of the political parties or individuals affected. He appealed to political parties, candidates and their supporters to reject inflammatory rhetoric, discourage violence and cooperate with security agencies to maintain public peace. Citing Section 40 of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, the Minority Leader reminded lawmakers that Nigerians were guaranteed the right to assemble freely and associate with others, including the right to form or belong to political parties. He also drew attention to the constitutional provision that makes the security and welfare of the people the primary purpose of government, stressing the need to protect citizens participating in legitimate political activities. Agbedi urged the House to invoke Section 88(1) of the Constitution, which empowers the National Assembly to investigate matters within its legislative competence and examine the conduct of public authorities responsible for administering relevant laws. To illustrate the growing concerns, he cited several incidents of political violence reported in different states. He recalled the disruption of political meetings in Enugu State on September 12, 2026, during which the police reportedly confirmed that two attendees were injured, while one person was allegedly killed. He also cited an attack on APC supporters travelling to a rally in Katsina State on October 28, 2026, which led to the arrest of 14 suspects. In Nasarawa State, Agbedi recalled an attack on an APC rally in Lafia on November 4, 2026, where several people were reportedly injured. He further mentioned a violent incident during a political procession in Asaba, Delta State, on November 7, 2026, in which the police reportedly confirmed that one person was killed and five others injured. The lawmaker warned that continued attacks, intimidation and destruction of property linked to political activities could result in further loss of lives and injuries. item.title: ‘Not the solution’, ‘ludicrous’, Man Utd legends, English pundits react to Carrick’s sacking
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Manchester United have sacked Michael Carrick after days of speculation over his future, following the club’s poor start to the Premier League season. The decision came after United’s hierarchy reviewed the team’s performances and considered possible replacements, with Mauricio Pochettino lined up for the job. But before the dismissal on Thursday, some prominent voices had questioned whether sacking Carrick would solve United’s problems, while others argued he should have been allowed to stay. United legends questioned whether a sacking would solve the problems Former United captain Gary Neville said changing managers would not address the club’s deeper issues. Speaking to NBC Sports, he warned that United risked repeating a cycle of brief improvement followed by a return to poor performances. Neville said eight managerial changes in 12 years showed that replacing the head coach alone was “not the answer”. He pointed to poor recruitment, weaknesses in the performance department and a lack of strong leadership throughout the club. Joined by his brother Gary on NBC Sports , former United defender Phil Neville focused on the defence after the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa, saying the back four that finished the match was not good enough for the Premier League and could get a manager sacked. Roy Keane had also criticised Carrick’s comments on Sky Sports after the Villa game, saying the head coach “talks a lot but doesn’t say much”. Keane questioned what would change if United continued conceding goals and chances. Paul Scholes, meanwhile, had looked ahead to United’s next appointment. Speaking on The Good, The Bad and The Football, he backed Antonio Conte over Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann, while warning that Conte would come with “a big warning”. Other English pundits have their say as Carragher calls the prospect of sacking Carrick ‘ludicrous’ Former Liverpool captain Jamie Carragher had called the prospect of dismissing Carrick “ludicrous” before the decision was made. He argued Carrick should help United through a difficult period before the club appointed a top-level manager in the summer. Jamie Redknapp had earlier said the squad lacked the quality and structure needed to turn the season around, adding that Carrick needed help with the players available to him. Former England international Chris Waddle, speaking after United’s draw with Tottenham in September, said the team had lost confidence and needed to rebuild it. item.title: Triton cabin crew’s medical certificate invalid during mid-air door incident – NSIB
item.description: By Dickson Omobola Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau, NSIB, has disclosed that the flight crew of a Bombardier Challenger 604 aircraft, with nationality and registration marks T7-SEI, operated by Triton Aviation Limited, observed an abnormal increase in cabin altitude and suspected a pressurisation issue at 17:19, before its passenger-crew door detached during initial climb. NSIB also revealed that the cabin crew’s medical certificate was not valid at the time of that occurrence. Recall that on October 15, 2026, the serious incident occurred after the aircraft took-off from Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja. The aircraft, operating as DWC052, was conducting a non-scheduled flight from Abuja to Murtala Muhammed International Airport, Lagos, with nine persons on board, comprising two flight crew members, one cabin crew member and six passengers. NSIB, in its preliminary report, stated that the captain subsequently instructed the cabin crew to double-check the main cabin door, adding that as the cabin crew approached the passenger-crew door to carry out the inspection, the door opened and subsequently detached from the aircraft. Director-General/Chief Executive Officer of NSIB, Captain Alex Badeh Jr, who signed the report, stated that the flight crew subsequently declared an emergency and coordinated with Abuja Air Traffic Control, ATC, for an immediate return to the airport. The report reads: “The aircraft landed safely on Runway 22 at approximately 17:34 local time. All nine occupants disembarked without injury. The aircraft sustained substantial damage. “Following notification of the occurrence on the same day, the NSIB immediately deployed investigators to the site to search for and recover the detached door, and commenced post-occurrence assessments. The detached door was subsequently recovered from a cornfield in Gui Village, Abuja Municipal Area Council, approximately five miles southwest of the airport. “The bureau reiterates that the preliminary report contains the factual information established during the investigation to date, including initial findings based on the evidence currently available and immediate safety recommendations arising from safety issues identified at this stage of the investigation. The report does not include analysis or conclusions regarding the causes or contributing factors associated with the occurrence, as the investigation remains ongoing. The bureau will publish its final report, including its analysis, conclusions, and further safety recommendations where appropriate, upon completion of the investigation in accordance with ICAO Annex 13 to the Convention on International Civil Aviation.” The post Triton cabin crew’s medical certificate invalid during mid-air door incident – NSIB appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Kano APC group mobilizes non-indigenes for Tinubu, Abba Yusuf
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Members of the All Progressives Congress APC in Kano State have begun mobilising non-indigenes living in the state to vote for President Bola Tinubu and Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf in the 2027 general elections. They inaugurated a political support group, Asiwaju Kano for Asiwaju Jagaban (AKA), which is led by Kogi lawmaker, Hon. Leke Abejide and has set for itself a target of at least 1.5 million votes for Tinubu’s re-election. The Chairman of the AKA Planning Committee, Hon. Ekundayo Emmanuel, said at the inauguration in Kano that coordinators had been installed in all 44 local government areas of the state. “Today, we are inaugurating coordinators across all 44 local government areas. Our responsibility is to mobilise at least one million five hundred thousand votes from non-indigenes residing across Kano State for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, our esteemed governor and leader, the people’s governor, Engineer Abba Kabir Yusuf, popularly known as Abba Gida Gida, as well as all APC candidates in the state,” he said. Emmanuel said the group was established to promote the political vision of Tinubu and Yusuf, adding that structures were being put in place to meet its target. The Kano State Coordinator of AKA, Hon. Seyi Olorunsola, commended Abejide, who represents Yagba East and Yagba West Federal Constituency of Kogi State in the House of Representatives, for returning to Kano, which he described as the lawmaker’s place of origin, to give back to its communities. Olorunsola said Abejide had recently empowered more than 300,000 people in Kano, including nearly 5,000 widows. He said each beneficiary received N50,000, alongside bags of rice and wrappers. According to him, other politicians who rose to prominent positions through their connections to Kano had not undertaken similar initiatives to support communities in the state. He said Abejide’s decision to return and contribute to the welfare of residents showed his commitment to giving back to his roots. The Special Adviser to Governor Yusuf on Information and Communication Technology, Yusuf Sharada, reiterated the state government’s commitment to inclusiveness, saying Kano considers everyone living in the state a citizen, irrespective of place of origin. He described Kano as home to people from different ethnic and cultural backgrounds and encouraged them to keep contributing to its development. Speaking on behalf of the Yoruba community and other ethnic groups, the Chairman of the Yoruba Community in Kano, Olajide Johnson Ogunleye, called on members to treat the mobilisation exercise as a collective responsibility and work towards the group’s target. He urged them to take the message to their respective communities and rally support for the APC candidates. “It is a duty and a call to action for every one of us to ensure that this vision becomes achievable. item.title: Nobody defended Peter Obi like Yunusa Tanko in the North — Shehu Sani
item.description: Former Kaduna Central Senator, Shehu Sani, has said Yunusa Tanko was one of the strongest advocates of Peter Obi in northern Nigeria, following his departure from the Obidient Movement and appointment to the Social Democratic Party’s 2027 presidential campaign council. Sani expressed surprise at Tanko’s decision to part ways with Obi, given his commitment to promoting the former Labour Party presidential candidate in the North. In a post on X on Wednesday, the former lawmaker wrote: “Nobody in the Northern part of River Niger has fanatically defended and promoted Dr Peter like Dr Yunusa Tanko. What must have happened for Dr Yunusa to part ways with Dr Peter? Anyway, nothing is impossible in politics.” Tanko, who previously coordinated the Obidient Movement, was on Wednesday named national coordinator of the SDP Presidential Campaign Council for the 2027 election. His appointment was announced at the inauguration of the party’s campaign council in Abuja, where he pledged to work with its presidential candidate, Adewale Adebayo, and running mate, Usman Bugaje, towards securing victory at the polls. Explaining his political realignment, Tanko said he resigned as political adviser (North) to Obi on October 30. He linked the decision to his appointment to the leadership of the National Consultative Front (NCFront), following the death of its former co-chairman and ex-Speaker of the House of Representatives, Ghali Na’Abba. Tanko also disclosed that he had contacted Obi and the National Democratic Congress leader, Seriake Dickson, to inform them of his decision. He acknowledged their support during his time as coordinator of the Obidient Movement and expressed appreciation for their contributions. The SDP campaign coordinator said his relationship with Adebayo predated the latest appointment, adding that they had worked together since 2023 and shared a commitment to building a better Nigeria. He also described the SDP as a left-wing, people-oriented party that represents the interests of ordinary Nigerians, particularly those he said had been neglected. item.title: Zamfara APC declares Hassan Dangaladima winner of rerun primary
item.description: By Idris Salisu, Gusau The All Progressives Congress (APC) has declared Hassan Umar Dangaladima winner of the rerun primary election for the Birnin Magaji/Kaura-Namoda Federal Constituency of Zamfara State. Dangaladima polled 9,416 votes to defeat his challenger, Aminu Sani Jaji, who scored 661 votes in the exercise. The result was announced in Gusau by Mustapha Muhammad, Acting Chairman of the APC Electoral Committee from the party’s National Headquarters, in the presence of party leaders and other stakeholders. Muhammad said the committee, having concluded its assessment of the exercise, was satisfied that Dangaladima secured the highest number of votes and was therefore duly declared winner of the rerun primary. Speaking shortly after his declaration, Dangaladima pledged to provide effective and meaningful representation for the constituency if elected to the House of Representatives in the 2027 general election. He called on APC members and supporters to unite behind him and other candidates of the party ahead of the polls. He also urged party supporters to work towards the success of the APC in the forthcoming general election. item.title: N10.8trn borrowing must deliver infrastructure, jobs – Agbese
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The Deputy Spokesperson of the House of Representatives, Philip Agbese, has urged the Federal Government to sustain effective budget implementation to translate Nigeria’s improving economic indicators into tangible benefits for citizens. Agbese, who represents Ado/Okpokwu/Ogbadigbo Federal Constituency of Benue State, said the proposed N10.8 trillion external borrowing must translate into infrastructure development, job creation and improved living conditions for Nigerians. He made the call while speaking with journalists in Abuja on Thursday, following the release of the Federal Government’s Second Quarter 2026 Budget Implementation Report and President Bola Tinubu’s request for National Assembly approval of a fresh external borrowing plan. Tinubu had on Wednesday written to the House of Representatives, seeking approval to implement the external borrowing plan contained in the 2026 Appropriation Act to finance budgeted projects and consolidate the macroeconomic gains recorded by his administration. The Budget Implementation Report, released by the Budget Office of the Federation on November 7, showed that government revenue stood at approximately N11.9 trillion in the first half of 2026. The report also indicated that Nigeria’s economy grew by 4.43 per cent in the second quarter, its strongest quarterly expansion since the third quarter of 2024, while nominal Gross Domestic Product rose to N119.29 trillion. The growth was attributed to improved crude oil production and resilient activities in the non-oil sector. Reacting to the figures, Agbese commended the Ministers of Finance and Budget and Economic Planning, Taiwo Oyedele and Abubakar Atiku Bagudu, respectively, for their roles in strengthening fiscal coordination and improving budget performance. He said the figures underscored the importance of effective fiscal management, improved revenue generation and coordination in implementing national development priorities. “These numbers show that deliberate efforts are being made to improve the management of our economy. We must acknowledge the work being done by the Ministers of Finance and Budget and Economic Planning to strengthen fiscal coordination and ensure that national priorities are reflected in government spending. “While there is still considerable work to be done, we should be able to recognise progress where it is being made. The figures indicate that the economy is responding to ongoing reforms, and the responsibility before us is to sustain that momentum,” he said. The Labour Party lawmaker said collaboration between the two ministers was important to achieving the administration’s economic objectives, particularly in strengthening revenue generation, managing public expenditure and directing available resources towards critical sectors. item.title: Video: Thugs attack NDC supporters in Lagos
item.description: Suspected political thugs, on Thursday, invaded a rally in Oregun, along Kudirat Abiola Way, Ikeja, Lagos, organised by the Nigerian Democratic Congress, NDC, supporters. Read Also: Explainer: What INEC’s 2023 results in Lagos, Oyo, Osun actually reveal The rally was part of a townhall meeting organised by NDC in the ongoing campaign for the presidential candidate of the NDC, Peter Obi, and governorship candidate, Funsho Doherty. The rampaging thugs attacked supporters, with some sustaining injuries in the process. The hoodlums, armed with cutlasses, cudgels and stones, invaded the venue of the event, disrupted proceedings and sent participants scampering for safety. Though Obi was said not to be at the rally when the incident occurred, it was gathered that the thugs demanded money from the NDC supporters for holding the rally. When their demands were not met, the thugs resorted to attacking anyone on sight. A police source, who spoke on condition of anonymity, confirmed the attack. The source said the organisers did not obtain prior approval before the event. “Yes, it happened. However, it’s unfortunate that the organisers did not inform the security agencies of their rally,” the source said. Below is a video from the scene: Thugs attack NDC supporters in Lagos Suspected political thugs, on Thursday, invaded a rally at Kudirat Abiola Way, Ikeja, Lagos, organised by the Nigerian Democratic Congress, NDC, supporters. pic.twitter.com/ngB7LmAliR — Vanguard Newspapers (@vanguardngrnews) November 12, 2026 Vanguard News The post Video: Thugs attack NDC supporters in Lagos appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: City Boy Movement targets 500,000 Enugu students for Tinubu
item.description: By Chinedu Adonu The City Boy Movement has launched a membership registration drive across tertiary institutions in Enugu State, targeting 500,000 students as part of its mobilisation efforts for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election in 2027. The South-East Zonal Coordinator of the movement’s Membership Registration and Data Management, Dr. Onyeka Nwafor, disclosed this during a membership registration exercise in Enugu. Nwafor said the movement had partnered with the Council of Students’ Union Government Presidents in Enugu State (COSPEN) to expand its membership base and mobilise students across campuses in support of Tinubu’s second-term ambition. He said the initiative was aimed at strengthening the movement’s presence in the South-East and demonstrating student support for the President’s administration. Also speaking, the COSPEN Chairman and President of the Students’ Union Government of the Institute of Management and Technology (IMT), Enugu, Comrade Emmanuel Nwankwo, said student leaders had endorsed Tinubu’s re-election bid, citing the impact of the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND). Nwankwo pledged that the council would mobilise more than 500,000 students for the registration exercise. He spoke during a meeting with Nwafor at Tiger Bar, Enugu, where both parties discussed strategies for expanding membership registration and improving coordination across campuses. “Many of our peers would have dropped out of school because of financial constraints, but NELFUND has eased the burden on parents and helped students remain in school. For this, we believe Mr President deserves a second term,” he said. Describing COSPEN as the gatekeepers of tertiary institutions in the state, Nwankwo said the student loan scheme had helped address some of the financial difficulties confronting students. Nwafor, a former governorship aspirant of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Anambra State, said the movement was determined to expand its presence across tertiary institutions in the South-East. “We have resolved to scale up registration across campuses in Enugu. The registration exercise will demonstrate the level of student support for President Tinubu’s administration, particularly the impact of the student loan initiative,” he said. He added that COSPEN would coordinate the mobilisation exercise through student union presidents across the various institutions. item.title: Nigeria, Jamaica advance talks on bilateral aviation agreement
item.description: By Dickson Omobola Following a meeting between the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, and the Jamaican High Commissioner to Nigeria, Lincoln Downer, Nigeria and Jamaica are set to strengthen bilateral aviation relations as both countries move closer to concluding and signing their reviewed Bilateral Air Services Agreement, BASA. Disclosing details of the meeting in a statement, Special Adviser on Media and Communications to the Minister, Tunde Moshood, said the meeting focused on the finalisation of the existing BASA between the two countries, with particular emphasis on enhancing air travel, improving connectivity and creating a stronger framework for aviation cooperation between both countries. Moshood stated that the agreement had undergone extensive legal and technical reviews by officials of both countries, with the respective teams working to perfect the necessary documentation ahead of its formal endorsement. According to him, during the meeting, Downer expressed satisfaction with the progress made so far, noting that both countries had reached a critical stage in the process and were now looking towards setting a date for the signing. He was quoted to have said: “We are pleased now that we are at the point where we can now sign. We shared the legally reviewed text with your team, so I haven’t heard from them. That’s what I wanted to know today, where we stand, so that we can then set the date. You can give us an update?” The statement added: “In response, Keyamo requested the relevant file to ascertain the status of the documentation. He was briefed that the agreement had already undergone the necessary review by the Office of the Attorney-General of the Federation and had been returned, with the process now at an advanced stage of completion. “The Minister subsequently directed that a final copy of the agreement be made available to the Jamaican High Commissioner for a final review and proofreading to ensure that both parties are fully satisfied with the text before proceeding to the signing. “Both sides are now working towards agreeing on a mutually convenient date for the formal endorsement, tentatively scheduled to take place in Kingston, Jamaica, either in the last week of November or the first week of December 2026.” The post Nigeria, Jamaica advance talks on bilateral aviation agreement appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Chinese woman accused of spying on Nvidia chief entered Taiwan 8 times
item.description: The woman accused of spying for Beijing during an affair with Nvidia founder Jensen Huang visited Taiwan a total of eight times in 2024 and 2025, a Taiwanese government minister said Thursday. Taiwan, a dominant player in the global semiconductor industry, sits at the centre of strategic competition between the United States and China, which claims the self-ruled island as part of its territory. Jensen Huang, chief executive of the US-based chip giant Nvidia, has admitted to having an extramarital affair, reportedly with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed who US officials believe was working for Chinese intelligence. Beijing has rejected the spying allegations. Alice Huang, who is also known as Huang Le, used a Hong Kong passport to enter Taiwan “under a standard business visitor status” and there were “no special flags” about her at the time, Mainland Affairs Council (MAC) Minister Chiu Chui-cheng told lawmakers. Chiu made the remarks in Taiwan’s parliament in response to lawmakers’ questions about Alice Huang’s entries into Taiwan and a New York Times report that the United States had advised Taiwan as early as 2024 to monitor her movements. “At least we at the Mainland Affairs Council did not receive any relevant information,” Chiu said. “If we had, we definitely would have stepped up our entry screening and border flow management.” Chiu said records show that Alice Huang visited Taiwan three times in 2024 and five times in 2025. The records do not show any entries for this year, he said. “If we had any of the kind of critical intelligence you mentioned, leading us to believe she posed a threat to Taiwanese society, we would have definitely flagged her for heightened review,” Chiu said. “For any case where there are doubts, we intensify the level of scrutiny, and if we determine there are security concerns, there is no way we would allow her to enter the country.” The government has said Taiwan’s security agencies are investigating the incident. Cabinet spokeswoman Michelle Lee said Thursday “there is currently no public information” about whether Alice Huang “is suspected of any criminal offence or on the related investigative procedures”. “If a criminal offence is involved, due to the principle of prosecutorial confidentiality during an ongoing investigation, we cannot provide any further comment,” Lee said. Alice Huang was seen at a dinner in May 2025 hosted by Jensen Huang at a Chinese restaurant in Taipei during Computex, the island’s top tech expo. Journalists stood outside the restaurant filming through glass windows and doors as Jensen Huang and a woman identified as Alice Huang, who was wearing a pink dress, mingled with other attendees. At one point, Jensen Huang can be seen putting his arm around Alice Huang as she kisses him on the right cheek, press livestreams show. item.title: Two French Guards Collapse As Macron Welcomes Slovak President
item.description: Two members of France’s elite Republican Guard collapsed almost simultaneously outside the Elysee Palace as President Emmanuel Macron welcomed his Slovak counterpart, according to televised images and a presidential source. As is customary for the arrival of foreign heads of state, the Republican Guards formed an honour guard in full ceremonial dress with sabres for the arrival of Slovak President Peter Pellegrini late Wednesday. One guard can be seen swaying before crashing to the ground, falling against a pillar at the Elysee Palace as his ceremonial sword clattered to the ground. France’s President Emmanuel Macron (R) bids farewell to Slovakia’s President Peter Pellegrini following their meeting at the Elysee presidential Palace in Paris on November 11, 2026. (Photo by Guillaume Saligot / AFP) | Guillaume Saligot / AFP Aides and Macron immediately rushed towards the stricken guard, images from an AFP photographer showed. Le Parisien daily said that a second guard collapsed off camera, with Macron looking concerned and then hurriedly welcoming his Slovak counterpart. A French presidential source, who asked not to be named, told AFP that both guards had suffered from “fainting attacks” and no other comment would be made. “Both of them were swiftly taken care of, and everything is fine,” added the source. The Republican Guard, part of the French gendarmerie, is responsible for guards of honour in France, which often involve standing for long periods in heavy clothing while holding their sword vertically. France’s President Emmanuel Macron (L) and other officials attend to a Republican Guard who fainted while standing at attention, as he waits the arrival of Slovakia’s President at the Elysee Palace in Paris on November 11, 2026. (Photo by Guillaume Saligot / AFP) | Guillaume Saligot / AFP AFP The post Two French Guards Collapse As Macron Welcomes Slovak President appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: How Starring in ‘Clarissa’ Reunited Sophie Okonedo With Her Nigerian Roots After Two Decades
item.description: Sophie Okonedo has spent three decades pursuing demanding roles, occasionally stepping away from steady work for years while waiting for independent scripts to secure financing. Now, two of those projects, the American coming-of-age drama Mouse and the Lagos-set literary adaptation Clarissa, are arriving within months of each other, including one that prompted an unexpected personal reckoning. Okonedo stars in the title role of Clarissa , a contemporary reimagining of Virginia Woolf’s 1925 novel Mrs. Dalloway relocated from post-war London to modern-day Lagos and Abraka, Delta State. Written and directed by Nigerian twin filmmakers Arie and Chuko Esiri ( Eyimofe ), the film examines the insulated lives of Nigeria’s wealthy elite while offering the British-Nigerian Oscar nominee a chance to reconnect with her father’s homeland more than 20 years after her last visit. Bridging a 20-Year Gap in Lagos Raised in London by her mother, Okonedo admitted that accepting the role forced her to confront a long-standing estrangement from her Nigerian roots. Prior to principal photography in November and December 2025, she had not stepped foot in Nigeria in over two decades. “I said to Chuko, ‘You know, I was estranged from my family there, and I don’t know if I really know Nigeria well enough,'” Okonedo said in a recent interview reflecting on the production. “‘It’s been a big gap. I didn’t grow up there and I was brought up by my mother, so it’s a sticky area for me. I don’t know how I’ll be able to do it.'” According to Okonedo, Chuko Esiri offered a simple reassurance: “‘Don’t worry, if nothing else, we will bridge that for you.'” Rather than checking into a hotel during the Lagos shoot, Okonedo lived at the home of the directors’ mother—a decision that grounded her both personally and professionally. “I thought, ‘Oh, I’m going to go on a sort of voyage here of discovery,’ and—I mean, I could get emotional talking about it—it lived up to that and more,” she said. “I got very comfortable at Chuko’s mum’s house, and then for the filming, I just didn’t move into the hotel. I just stayed there the whole time.” Nigerian co-director Arie Esiri (R) and Nigerian co-director and screenwriter Chuko Esiri pose for a portrait session on the sidelines of the 79th edition of the Cannes Film Festival in Cannes, southern France, on May 17, 2026. (Photo by JULIE SEBADELHA / AFP) Reimagining Virginia Woolf Among Nigeria’s Elite The Esiri brothers first approached Okonedo in 2021—before showing her a finished screenplay, having written the older Clarissa specifically with her in mind. Having seen their 2020 debut feature, Eyimofe (This Is My Desire) , Okonedo agreed immediately. “They said at the time, ‘We have this idea about doing an adaptation of Virginia Woolf’s Mrs. Dalloway , and reimagining it in Nigeria.’ And I immediately went, ‘I’m doing it,'” she recalled. “I don’t know when in my lifetime I’d get a chance to work in Nigeria and to be doing an art house film there

item.title: Five key allies of Peter Obi who parted ways with him after 2023
item.description: ‎ The recent decision by Yunusa Tanko a leading figure in the Obidient Movement, to accept an appointment as Director-General of the presidential campaign council of the Social Democratic Party (SDP) candidate has once again drawn attention to the growing list of notable political associates who have distanced themselves from former Labour Party presidential candidate, Peter Obi. ‎ ‎Since the conclusion of the 2023 presidential election, Obi has remained one of the country’s most influential opposition politicians. ‎However, several key figures who played important roles in his campaign, political structure, or movement have either left the Labour Party, aligned with other political interests, or openly criticized his political direction. Obi is presently the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate for the 2027 election. ‎ ‎These defections have triggered renewed debate about the cohesion of the political movement that emerged around Obi’s 2023 presidential campaign. 2027: IGP warns officers against compromise Thugs attack Pantami’s campaign rally in Gombe ‎ ‎While Obi continues to command a loyal support base across the country, the departure of several high-profile associates underscores the challenge of maintaining political unity and building a durable structure ahead of the next electoral cycle. ‎ However, his present alliance with Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, the leader of Kwankwasiyya Movement, is seen by many as a plus to him. ‎ ‎Below are five of such most prominent names. ‎ ‎ YUNUSA TANKO tanko yunusa ‎ ‎Perhaps the latest and most symbolic departure is that of Yunusa Tanko, who served as National Coordinator of the Obidient Movement and was one of the most visible defenders of Obi after the 2023 election. ‎ ‎Tanko was a key mobiliser of Obi’s support base across the country and regularly represented the movement on national television and at political events. item.title: ACF crisis deepens
item.description: Moves to resolve the lingering supremacy battle within the ranks of the Arewa Consultative Forum (ACF) have yet to produce results after a closed-door meeting by members of the Board of Trustees (BoT), the National Executive Committee (NEC) and some first-class emirs from the northern region ended in what some sources described as “deadlock.” Daily Trust learnt that the meeting, which took place on Tuesday at the private residence of the Sultan of Sokoto, Alhaji Muhammadu Sa’ad Abubakar III, in Maitama, Abuja, lasted two hours between 5pm and 7pm without any tangible resolutions reached. The traditional rulers at the meeting included the Etsu Nupe, Alhaji Yahaya Abubakar, and the Aku Uka of Wukari, Dr. Manu Ishaku Adda Ali. The Sultan was reportedly not at the meeting as he was attending to other matters of national importance somewhere. Although the details of the meeting, which was convened at the instance of the Sultan, were sketchy, sources privy to the happenings in the ACF confided in Daily Trust that the gathering focused on resolving the worsening division in the leadership of the northern socio-political group. One of the sources said both the Etsu Nupe and the Aku Uka expressed serious reservations over the inability of the BoT and NEC to arrive at a neutral ground and work together towards finding solution to the security and economic challenges afflicting the North. “In fact, one of the emirs alluded to the fact that the North is now a laughing stock…That we cannot speak with one voice at a critical moment of our existence,” he said. Our correspondents report that the meeting on Tuesday was a continuation of series of engagements with contending parties (NEC and BoT) towards resolving the protracted leadership crisis occasioned by alleged financial impropriety. Daily Trust learnt that the Sultan, with the support of the Emir of Lafia, Justice Sidi Dauda Bage Muhammad and other northern traditional rulers have been having talks with the ACF leaders since the beginning of 2026 when the BoT and NEC engaged in blame game. On one hand, the Chairman of the BoT, Alhaji Bashir Dalhatu, with the support of some members, had asked the Secretary General of the organisation, Malam Murtala Aliyu, to leave. But Murtala had kicked saying his tenure will expire in December 2026. He reportedly has the support of some members, including the Chairman of the NEC, Barrister Mamman Mike Osuman, SAN. Besides the leadership tussle, the lodgement of about N3.9 billion donated to the ACP in a new account at JAIZ Bank, rather than in any of the main accounts of the organisation in First Bank, United Bank for Africa (UBA) and Unity Bank, has caused disaffection among members. During its 25th anniversary celebration held in November 2025, some notable northern leaders and businessmen donated the amount, in addition to pledges that are yet to be redeemed. Also, there was nearly N700 million donated by some northern leaders in order to organise the 25th anniversary
